newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields higher, ponder next move.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields higher, ponder next move.

text.p: *Australian bond yields remained higher, particularly at the short end where speculative trades on a possible policy easing were closed out after the Reserve Bank made no announcement.
*Turnover thin ahead of U.S. jobs, Monday's local holiday.

Australian bond yields remained higher, particularly at the short end, where speculative trades on a possible easing in official interest rates were closed out after the Reserve Bank made no announcement.
There had been talk during offshore trading hours that the central bank was about to ease policy in the wake of Wednesday's first quarter GDP and after Tuesday's board meeting.

However, such speculation appeared to be having a greater impact on the Australian dollar, which remained pegged well below US$0.7600 even after the RBA remained silent at its usual 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) announcement time.
Rate cut talk is likely to keep the market on its toes in the coming weeks, it having been caught completely on the hop when the RBA last eased to 5.5 percent on May 23.
"People will be watching their screens at 9.30 (a.m.) day in, day out, until it becomes clear that an easing is not on the cards," one trader said.
The market may get some clues on policy when RBA governor Ian Macfarlane addresses a conference in London at around 1.50 a.m. local time (1550 GMT).
In the meantime, the market is likely to stay quiet ahead of Friday's U.S. payrolls data and Monday's local holiday.

The market generally underperforms against the dollar bloc, notably against the short-end of the New Zealand curve, despite quarterly N.Z. private sector wages rising a slightly stronger than expected 1.1 percent. The local yield curve flattened in the absence of a RBA monetary policy announcement.
